title: Force a status re-read after a hub write so controls stop snapping back for up to a minute
why_top: correctness-2 tops the board on both metrics that matter and is the only top-three idea carrying no open concern. Adjusted 15.5 beats frontend-cards-7 (14.5) and offline-8 (14.3), and per_round 7.8 beats 7.3 and 7.2 — the two metrics agree, so no tie-break was needed. Both rivals sit on a live −2 dock (C3, C4) for unresolved implementation hazards; correctness-2's only concern, C1's session-churn objection, was resolved in round 2 with a firsthand read showing the extra read is one control-channel multipleRequest on the existing client, not a login or an 8800 session — which matters more here than anywhere else, because the hardware brief says this hub wedges under repeated auth. I re-verified the premise myself: hub_control.py:37-39 schedules an unconditional async_request_refresh after every successful write, and coordinator.py:753 gates the status read behind `if self._polls % self._status_every == 0`, where _status_every is `max(1, round(STATUS_MAX_AGE / interval))` (coordinator.py:112, STATUS_MAX_AGE=60 at const.py:155). The confirming poll therefore usually skips the very read that would confirm the write, and grepping the component for _force_status returns nothing — no escape hatch exists today.
value_rationale: Like the 85-anchor — a verified, user-visible defect with a small, trivially revertible fix — but three deltas move it down: no pinning test exists today (nothing in tests/ constructs H500HubSwitch or calls apply(), so the test must be written from scratch), the change touches two files rather than one, and the harm is a stale control that self-corrects within about 60 seconds rather than a crash or data loss → 68.
decomposition: Add a one-shot flag on the coordinator (e.g. self._force_status = False, set next to self._polls in __init__) and widen the gate at coordinator.py:753 to `if self._force_status or self._polls % self._status_every == 0:`, clearing the flag inside the branch so it fires exactly once.

In H500HubControl.apply (hub_control.py:37-39), set coordinator._force_status = True immediately before the existing await self.coordinator.async_request_refresh(); leave the comment about not polling per-call intact, since the fix adds no extra round trip beyond the one already scheduled.

Add one test to tests/test_coordinator.py that drives the flag directly rather than building an entity: set _polls and _status_every so the modulo would skip (test_coordinator.py:363 already manipulates both as plain attributes), set _force_status, run a poll, and assert hub_status was called and the flag is back to False.

Add the companion negative test: same setup without the flag, assert hub_status was NOT called — this is what pins the fix and keeps a later refactor from making the status read unconditional, which is the session churn C1 warned about.
Run tools/verify.sh and confirm the full suite is green before finishing.
premise_notes: Premise-holds, and I re-confirmed it firsthand at HEAD: the unconditional refresh at hub_control.py:37-39, the modulo gate at coordinator.py:753, the _status_every derivation at coordinator.py:112, STATUS_MAX_AGE=60 at const.py:155, and no _force_status anywhere in the component; separately, the disqualified security-2 left behind one real unreported defect worth re-proposing on its own merits — an out-of-range start_time raises out of preview.py:67, which sits outside every try, giving a 500 with a traceback on a view no test calls.
metrics_note: I trusted raw adjusted total. All three contenders were active in 2 of 3 rounds (about 67%, comfortably past the ~60% well-tested threshold) with one champion each, so no idea is materially less tested and raw is the fair comparison. Per_round agrees anyway — correctness-2 leads on both (15.5/7.8 versus 14.5/7.3 and 14.3/7.2) — and per_arg is identical to per_round for every contender since champion counts are all 1, so it carries no extra signal. No tie-break was needed; for the record correctness-2 would have lost a peak tie-break (8.0 against 8.5 for both rivals), which is exactly why I state the metric: its lead is consistency across both its rounds plus a clean concern ledger, not a single high-water argument.
strongest_dissent: C1, round 1: "Forcing a status read after every write may cost an extra hub round trip per switch/select/number change, which is the session churn the H500 hardware brief warns against — the fix is only cheap if the refresh poll would have happened anyway rather than adding one." It was answered in round 2 and I count it resolved, but it remains the sharpest thing said against the idea and it constrains the build: the flag must ride the refresh that apply() already schedules, never add a second one. The one genuinely standing objection is smaller and procedural — the round-3 premise check noted the test as originally worded needs an entity plus a hass stub, since nothing in tests/ ever constructs H500HubSwitch or calls apply(), which is why the decomposition drives the coordinator flag directly instead.

minority.why_lost: Lost by 1.0 adjusted (14.5 to 15.5) and by 0.5 per_round, entirely on its −2 dock for C3, which is still open: nothing in tests/test_cards.mjs asserts serialization, so a fix shipped as a plain reload or a correlation token instead of a pending-rerun flag would let two list_recordings calls fly at the hub concurrently — the exact traffic pattern _busy exists to prevent. On raw score alone (16.5) it led the board; the unresolved hazard is what cost it, and Idris Bello confirmed the constraint firsthand in round 2 at card.js:485-489.
minority.flip_condition: It wins if someone closes C3 before the build: demonstrate the fix as a pending-rerun flag (set a _pending marker on the early return, re-run _load once in the finally) together with a test in tests/test_cards.mjs that counts concurrent list_recordings calls and asserts at most one is ever in flight. That lifts the −2, restoring it to 16.5 adjusted and 8.3 per_round, ahead of correctness-2 on both metrics and on peak.
